# Analogy of Recursion

#### Course: Learn Recursion with JavaScript

## Analogy of Recursion

Before we dive into more coding examples, let's look at a real-world analogy to understand recursion.

Imagine you're in a queue, and there are some people ahead of you.

![A Queue](data:image/png;base64,)

Suppose you want to know your position in the queue. The only information you have right now is that your position is behind that of the person ahead of you (John).

![Your Position With Respect to John](data:image/png;base64,)

So, you must ask John what his position is.

![Ask John His Position](data:image/png;base64,)

Just like you, John also has no idea about his position. So, he asks the person in front of him.

This process continues until someone asks for the position of the first person, Emily. As there is no one ahead of Emily (base case), she is at position 1.

![Each Person Asks the Position Ahead](data:image/png;base64,)

Now, Emily gives her position to David. He adds 1 to Emily's position to calculate his position (2).

Now that David knows he is in position 2, he tells Betty about it.

Betty adds 1 to David's position and passes the information to John and so on.

![Each Person](data:image/png;base64,)

When John tells you his position (4), you can finally know your position by adding 1 to it, which is 5.
